title: The Circular Flow and What Breaks It: Moravia, Vienna, Bonn, Cambridge
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Textile Town and the Widow's Road

stops.name: Třešť, the manufacturer's son
stops.date_confidence: attested. The coordinate is the town's own, 49.29083 N / 15.48222 E; the research dossier carried 49.3167 / 15.4833, which sits about three kilometres north of Třešť in open country, and a third and different wrong pin elsewhere in the same dossier. The birth name is Joseph Alois Schumpeter: no source consulted gives a third forename Julius, which appears to be contamination from the maternal grandfather, Dr. Julius Grüner.
stops.campa: In a Moravian town of cloth mills, German-speaking and Czech-speaking in the same streets, Joseph Alois Schumpeter is born to Josef Schumpeter, textile manufacturer, and to Johanna Grüner, a doctor's daughter. He is an only child, and the third generation in the trade, and the last. The workshop and the family house stand within the same small compass of the square, and the boy's first world is a going concern: looms, orders, credit, the weekly arithmetic of a firm that must either grow or be overtaken by someone who has thought of something better.
suggested_refs: The Schumpeter birth house in Třešť, photographed and captioned as his rodný dům, with no plaque or museum confirmed in the sources consulted

stops.name: Třešť, the father dead before the boy is four
stops.date_confidence: date attested; cause not. The hunting accident given in most retellings could not be traced to a death record in this pass and is carried as tradition.
stops.campa: Josef Schumpeter dies on the fourteenth of January. His son is not yet four. The retellings that follow, one biographer copying the next, give the cause as a hunting accident, and no death record has been produced to confirm it. The shape it leaves is not in question: a young widow, a firm without its master, a boy who will grow up with no father to imitate, and a mother who will spend the next two decades manoeuvring him upward through a society that hands out places by birth. Johanna does not stay in Třešť.
sources: Deutsche Biographie, deutsche-biographie.de/sfz106815.html (date and the father as Josef, 1855-1887)
standard biographies, for the hunting-accident tradition; no primary death record located

stops.name: Graz, the widow's household
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day set to 01. The dossier's chronology wrongly attached the father's death to a move to Vienna; the move that followed the death was to Graz, in 1888.
stops.campa: Johanna moves with her son to Graz, capital of Styria, a garrison and university town where an educated widow with a small manufacturer's money can live respectably and be seen living respectably. Nothing of the family's Moravian standing counts in Graz; the address, the accent, the acquaintance list all have to be made again from nothing. He is five years old and already somebody's project. Twenty-three years later he will come back to this city holding its chair of political economy. For now he enters the Volksschule.

stops.name: Vienna, the Theresianum
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1893-1901; month and day set to 01. The move to Vienna followed the mother's remarriage, not the father's death six years earlier.
stops.campa: Johanna marries Sigismund von Kéler, a Feldmarschallleutnant more than thirty years her senior, and the marriage opens the door of the Theresianum: the imperial academy where the sons of the Habsburg nobility are prepared for the ministries, the diplomatic service and the officer corps. He enters at ten, as the stepson of the army. The manners taught there will be remarked on for the rest of his life, usually with irritation. He leaves at eighteen with Greek, Latin, French, English, Italian, the law of administration, and the manners.
suggested_refs: The Theresianum, Favoritenstraße 15, Vienna
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net
Deutsche Biographie (lists Kéler as stepfather from 1893)

stops.name: University of Vienna, the law faculty
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1901; month set to the start of the winter term. Pin inherited byte-identical from carl_menger.journey.json, the Ringstrasse main building occupied from 1884.
stops.campa: He enrols in law, because in the Austrian university economics is taught inside the law faculty and there is no other door into it. The Ringstrasse building he walks into is the one Carl Menger has lectured in since 1884, and Menger's Grundsätze of 1871, with its marginal utility and its refusal of the German historical school, is the floor everything here is built on. Schumpeter reads it early and will spend a lifetime writing about its author: in the Epochen, in the obituary essays, and last of all in the History of Economic Analysis.
suggested_refs: Carl Menger, Grundsätze der Volkswirthschaftslehre (1871), the doctrinal floor of the Vienna faculty Schumpeter enters
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net

stops.name: University of Vienna, Böhm-Bawerk's seminar
stops.date_confidence: attested. Pin inherited byte-identical from ludwig_von_mises.journey.json and eugen_von_bohm_bawerk.journey.json, both of which stage this room and name Schumpeter in it. The seminar is the teacher's scene on his own file; this stop is Schumpeter's own presence at the table.
stops.campa: In the private seminar of Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk, Habsburg finance minister and theorist of capital and interest, four students argue Marx across one table: Schumpeter, Ludwig von Mises, Otto Bauer, Rudolf Hilferding. The room is the teacher's, and the teacher sets the questions. Bauer will be foreign secretary of the Austrian republic, Hilferding twice a German finance minister, Schumpeter an Austrian one, Mises the last defender of a liberal order none of the other three will trouble to keep. They are all between twenty and twenty-five.
suggested_refs: Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk's private seminar, University of Vienna, staged as its own scene on the teacher's file
sources: eugen_von_bohm_bawerk.journey.json, stop 'Vienna, four men at one table'
ludwig_von_mises.journey.json, stop 'University of Vienna, Bohm-Bawerk's seminar'
History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net

stops.name: University of Vienna, the doctorate at twenty-three
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 1906; day set to 01.
stops.campa: He takes the doctorate in law in February, twenty-three years old, with economics as the real subject and the law as its container. Böhm-Bawerk and Friedrich von Wieser have taught him theory, Eugen von Philippovich policy. The Vienna he leaves is at the height of what it can produce and eight years from the end of the state that pays for it. He does not stay. Within months he is on a road that runs Berlin, Britain, Cairo, and he will hold no Austrian post at all until 1909.
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net

segments.name: Berlin, London, Cairo: The Years With No Post

stops.name: Berlin, Unter den Linden, the summer after the degree
stops.date_confidence: attested to summer 1906; day set to 01. This falls after the Vienna doctorate, not during his Vienna studies as the dossier's chronology had it: it is the opening leg of a post-doctoral tour.
stops.campa: Degree in hand, he goes to Berlin for the summer to study economics where it is done the other way: Schmoller's historical school, statistics and institutions and the long patient description of how a particular economy actually came to be, against the Viennese habit of deducing it from a few assumptions about wanting things. Schumpeter will spend his career refusing to pick a side, insisting that the quarrel between theory and history is a quarrel about the division of labour and nothing more. Berlin is the first leg of a tour with no post waiting at the end of it.
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net ('Summer 1906')

stops.name: London School of Economics, Houghton Street
stops.date_confidence: attested to the academic year 1906-1907; month set to the start of term. The riding in Hyde Park comes from the dossier's narrative of the British sojourn and is not independently corroborated here.
stops.campa: He attaches himself to the young school on Houghton Street, ostensibly to research English common law. The Theresianum polish is now doing work: an Austrian of no fortune moving through English society on manners and languages alone. He touches the Oxford and Cambridge circles, reads in the libraries, and takes up the horsemanship he will still be boasting about in Cambridge, Massachusetts, forty years later. The year ends and he still holds no post. What Britain gives him is a set of mornings in Hyde Park, riding among the people who ride there.
suggested_refs: Rotten Row, Hyde Park, the morning ride of the London season
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net ('affiliated with LSE, ostensibly researching English common law', 1906-1907)

stops.name: London, the marriage to Gladys Seaver
stops.date_confidence: year and city attested by Deutsche Biographie; de.wikipedia places it late in 1907, and month is set accordingly. The church or registry office is not documented in any source consulted, so the coordinate is a generic central-London point, not the venue. Hans Kelsen as best man is reported, not documented.
stops.campa: At the close of the British year he marries Gladys Ricarde Seaver, an Englishwoman about twelve years his senior and the daughter of an Anglican church dignitary. Hans Kelsen, the jurist, is reported to have stood as best man. She is his entry into the class whose manners he has been wearing since he was ten. Within six years the marriage will be over in everything but law, and on when the law ended it the authorities flatly contradict each other. He is twenty-four, holds no post, and has a book unfinished.
sources: Wolfgang Stolper, Joseph Alois Schumpeter: The Public Life of a Private Man (preview PDF, api.pageplace.de)

stops.name: Cairo, the princess's accounts and the first book
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1907-1909; month and day set to order the segment. The Egyptian princess as client appears only in the dossier and could not be confirmed. The exact office is unknown and the coordinate marks the legal and financial quarter generally.
stops.campa: He takes work in Cairo with an Italian law and finance house, in the quarter where European firms administer Egyptian money under a British occupation. The manuscript is what the record holds: Das Wesen und der Hauptinhalt der theoretischen Nationalökonomie, written there at twenty-five, in a foreign city, with no university within a thousand miles of him. The tradition holds that he also managed an Egyptian princess's affairs, cutting her tenants' rents and raising her income at the same time; it is the kind of story that attaches itself to him. Whether there was a princess at all, no source consulted can say.
suggested_refs: Das Wesen und der Hauptinhalt der theoretischen Nationalökonomie (1908), composed in Cairo
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net (Cairo legal work, 1907-1909)

stops.name: University of Vienna, the venia legendi
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1909; month and day set to 01. Pin inherited byte-identical from carl_menger.journey.json, the same Ringstrasse main building.
stops.campa: The Cairo book earns him the habilitation and the right to lecture, in the building where he had been a student three years earlier. The rank of Privatdozent pays nothing whatever; what it confers is eligibility, and eligibility is the whole of what he wants out of Vienna. He is twenty-six, has published a treatise most of his elders dislike, and has no intention of waiting for a chair to fall vacant in a city holding more qualified men than posts. The offer that arrives comes from the far eastern edge of the monarchy, eight hundred kilometres away, and he takes it.

segments.name: The Youngest Professor: Czernowitz and Graz

stops.name: Czernowitz, the chair at the eastern edge
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1909; month set to the start of his tenure. The pin marks the city, not the Residence of the Bukovinian Metropolitans that houses the present Chernivtsi National University: the university did not receive that building until 1955, so it is the wrong building for 1909. The Franz Joseph University of Schumpeter's day occupied premises in the centre.
stops.campa: The Franz Joseph University in Czernowitz, capital of Bukovina, is the monarchy's furthest German-language faculty, in a town where German, Romanian, Ruthenian, Polish and Yiddish are all spoken inside a few streets. Schumpeter arrives as extraordinary professor at twenty-six and conducts himself as though he had arrived in Vienna. The salary is small and the distance from anyone who could correct him is very large. He lectures in evening dress, keeps a horse and a servant, and gives the local professoriate a great deal to talk about.
suggested_refs: The memorial plaque at Chernivtsi marking Schumpeter's professorship at the Franz Joseph University, 1909-1911
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net
en.wikipedia.org, 'Residence of Bukovinian and Dalmatian Metropolitans' (1955 handover)

stops.name: Czernowitz, the librarian's challenge
stops.date_confidence: tradition, not record. No contemporaneous police, university or newspaper account has been located, and the Graz Schumpeter Centre's institutional history is silent on it. McCraw's own telling places it soon after his arrival, when he was twenty-six, which fixes it to 1909 rather than the dossier's c. 1910; month set to 01.
stops.campa: The story, told by his biographer Thomas McCraw and by nobody holding a document, runs like this. The university librarian refuses students access to the books the new professor has assigned. The new professor makes a scene. The librarian, offended, issues the challenge; they fight with sabres; Schumpeter takes a small slice out of the librarian's shoulder; the students get their books; and the two men are afterwards friends. It is the direction that most retellings get wrong. He did not challenge the librarian. The librarian challenged him.
sources: Harvard Business School Working Knowledge, 'Rediscovering Schumpeter: The Power of Capitalism' (2007), interview with Thomas McCraw
Graz Schumpeter Centre institutional history, silent on the episode

stops.name: Czernowitz, the circular flow and the new combinations
stops.date_confidence: the first edition is attested to 1911 and the writing at Czernowitz is attested; month and day set to 01 to place the writing before the Graz appointment of 30 October.
stops.campa: In Bukovina he writes the Theorie der wirtschaftlichen Entwicklung. Its first move is to build an economy that works perfectly and goes nowhere: the circular flow, every year repeating the last, every price covering every cost, no profit and no interest anywhere in it. Then he introduces the one figure the model cannot generate out of itself, the entrepreneur, who carries out new combinations, borrows the purchasing power to do it, and breaks the flow. Development is not growth. It is a discontinuity, and it arrives from inside.
stops.quote: Capitalism ... is by nature a form or method of economic change and not only never is but never can be stationary.
stops.quote_source: Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy (1942), ch. VII, restating in English thirty-one years later the proposition the Theorie sets out here
suggested_refs: Theorie der wirtschaftlichen Entwicklung, first edition 1911
sources: Schumpeter Centre, University of Graz, institutional history
History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net

stops.name: Graz, professor by Supreme Resolution
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Graz Schumpeter Centre's institutional history.
stops.campa: By imperial Supreme Resolution of the thirtieth of October he is made full professor of political economy at the Karl-Franzens-Universität, in the city his mother brought him to at five. He is twenty-eight, among the youngest full professors in Austria-Hungary, and he takes the chair over the opposition of Richard Hildebrand of the historical school. Two years on, Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk will publish a dynamic theory of interest, in the journal he himself edits, aimed straight at his old student's. For now he is the only economist in the faculty, carrying economics, policy, public finance and democracy in turn.
suggested_refs: Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk, 'Eine dynamische Theorie des Kapitalzinses', Zeitschrift für Volkswirtschaft, Sozialpolitik und Verwaltung, vol. 22 (1913), the teacher's rebuttal in print, staged as its own scene on the teacher's file
The Graz Schumpeter Centre für ökonomische und soziale Studien, founded 2005 at the same university

stops.name: Columbia University, the exchange professor at thirty
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1913-1914; month set to the start of the American term.
stops.campa: He crosses to New York as Austrian exchange professor and finds an American economics that already knows his name: Irving Fisher, Wesley Clair Mitchell, Frank Taussig of Harvard. Columbia gives him an honorary doctorate at thirty. He learns the country, the working language and the department manners he will need twenty years later, when he will need them permanently. The marriage begun in London ends here in everything but the paperwork, and on the paperwork Deutsche Biographie says 1920 and Wikipedia says 1925. Gladys does not come.
sources: Schumpeter Centre, University of Graz, institutional history
History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net

stops.name: Graz, the Epochen in Max Weber's Grundriss
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1914; month and day set to 01. That the Epochen appeared in Weber's series is documented economic historiography; max_weber.journey.json treats the Grundriss as a central late thread but never names Schumpeter, so the connection is stated here from the bibliographic record rather than from that file.
stops.campa: Max Weber is assembling the Grundriss der Sozialökonomik, the encyclopaedic survey of the social economy he will work at until his death and never finish. Schumpeter writes for it the Epochen der Dogmen- und Methodengeschichte, the whole history of economic doctrine and method compressed into a section of another man's series, and does it at thirty-one. It is the first draft of the project he will still be writing on the day he dies. That the Epochen stands in Weber's series is bibliography. What passed between the two men, the record consulted here does not show.
stops.quote: Actually, however, economists have never allowed their analysis to be influenced by the professional psychologists of their times, but have always framed for themselves such assumptions about psychical processes as they thought it desirable to make.
stops.quote_source: History of Economic Analysis (1954), Part I, ch. 4, sec. 2, pp. 27-28, the mature form of the project begun in the Epochen
suggested_refs: Epochen der Dogmen- und Methodengeschichte (1914), in Weber's Grundriss der Sozialökonomik

stops.name: Graz, the dean in the fourth year of the war
stops.date_confidence: the deanship is attested for the academic year 1916/17 by the Graz Schumpeter Centre; month set to the start of term. The memoranda to Emperor Karl urging peace, monetary reconstruction and a federal solution are NOT carried by that source, which mentions only the office; the dossier attached them to a citation that does not support them.
stops.campa: He holds the office of dean of the law faculty for the academic year, while the monarchy that appointed him is being taken apart by the war it began. The students are at the front, the currency is going, and the multinational space his own career was built out of, Moravia to Vienna to Bukovina to Styria, is dissolving into national claims that have no room in them for a man from everywhere. Accounts of memoranda he is said to have sent the Emperor, urging peace and a federal settlement, are not carried by the university's own record of his deanship.
stops.quote: In breaking down the pre-capitalist framework of society, capitalism thus broke not only barriers that impeded its progress but also flying buttresses that prevented its collapse.
stops.quote_source: Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy (1942), written twenty-six years after the collapse of the framework he served
sources: Schumpeter Centre, University of Graz, institutional history ('Schumpeter held the office of dean during the academic year 1916/17')

stops.name: Berlin, the Socialization Commission
stops.date_confidence: attested to late 1918; the first commission was established in November 1918 and ceased work in early April 1919, which bounds his service. Kautsky was co-chair with Ernst Francke of the Gesellschaft für Soziale Reform, not sole chair as the dossier had it. The meeting building is not documented and the coordinate marks the government quarter.
stops.campa: Six weeks after the Habsburg empire ends, the Council of People's Deputies in Berlin appoints a commission to decide which German industries are to be socialized and by what method. Karl Kautsky and Ernst Francke co-chair it. Rudolf Hilferding and Emil Lederer sit on it, both of them out of Böhm-Bawerk's Vienna seminar, and so does Schumpeter, who is not a socialist and is asked anyway. His position is compensated communal control of coal rather than confiscation. The commission stops work in April and settles nothing.
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net ('late 1918')

stops.name: Himmelpfortgasse, State Secretary for Finance
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: Karl Renner makes him finance minister of a republic of six million people that was an empire of fifty million four months ago. He is thirty-six. His programme is a single heavy progressive levy on capital to retire the war debt at one stroke, stabilization of the crown, refusal of immediate union with Germany, and the rebuilding of Vienna as the financial centre of the successor states. Every part of it has an enemy inside the cabinet, and the most effective of them is Otto Bauer, foreign secretary, who sat at the same seminar table with him fifteen years ago. The levy is never enacted.
stops.quote: An 'automatic' gold currency is part and parcel of a laissez-faire and free-trade economy...
stops.quote_source: History of Economic Analysis (ed. Elizabeth Boody Schumpeter, Oxford University Press, 1954); given by the reference work that reproduces it as a partial excerpt
suggested_refs: The Austrian Finance Ministry, Himmelpfortgasse 8, Vienna, the Winter Palace of Prince Eugene
sources: schumpeter.info bibliography index of ministerial speeches and programmes
ludwig_von_mises.journey.json (Bauer and Schumpeter at the same seminar)

stops.name: Vienna, the Alpine Montan shares
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The covert currency operation and the accusation are reported and a later investigation is said to have found no personal wrongdoing, but no primary investigative record was consulted in this pass. Month and day set to order the segment.
stops.campa: The charge, made at the time and repeated since, is that the finance minister used the financier Richard Kola in confidential operations to support the currency, and encouraged an Italian purchase of a controlling block of Alpine Montangesellschaft shares in order to place Austria's largest steel and coal concern beyond the reach of Bauer's socialization plan. The method is not in dispute: a minister running policy through private financiers, outside the books, against his own cabinet. He is later said to have been cleared of enriching himself. No investigative file has been produced either way.
sources: research dossier synthesis of the documented allegation and later exoneration; no primary investigative record consulted

stops.name: Vienna, out with the cabinet
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The dossier's wording, that the government was replaced, is wrong: Renner stayed chancellor. The Renner II cabinet resigned on 17 October 1919 after ratification of the Treaty of Saint-Germain, and Renner III was elected the same day, without Schumpeter.
stops.campa: On the seventeenth of October the Renner cabinet resigns, the Treaty of Saint-Germain having been ratified and the borders of the rump state settled at last. Renner forms his third government the same day. Schumpeter is not in it, and he never holds public office again, in any country. Seven months of it: no capital levy passed, the crown still falling, and a name among Social Democrats for unreliability and among Christian Socials for something worse. He is thirty-six years old.

segments.name: The Banker: Credit, New Combinations, Ruin

stops.name: Innere Stadt, the Biedermann Bank
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1921. The exact founding date of 26 July 1921 and the figure of about 240 employees come from Peneder and Resch's 2025 archival study, which sits behind a publisher authentication redirect and could not be fetched in this pass; both are carried as reported, not confirmed. The premises are not documented and the pin marks the historic banking quarter.
stops.campa: The old private house of M. L. Biedermann is converted into a joint-stock bank and Schumpeter is made its president, with the right to conduct business on his own account. He is now positioned to do the thing his book describes: put created credit into the hands of men carrying out new combinations, and finance the discontinuity himself. He also keeps a salon, keeps horses, and spends a very long way past what the presidency pays him. By 1923 the bank employs some two hundred and forty people.
stops.quote: the function of entrepreneurs is to reform or revolutionize the pattern of production by exploiting an invention or, more generally, an untried technological possibility for producing a new commodity or producing an old one in a new way...
stops.quote_source: Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy (1942), ch. XII; the definition the bank presidency is an attempt to finance
suggested_refs: M. L. Biedermann & Co. Bankaktiengesellschaft, Innere Stadt, Vienna
sources: Michael Peneder and Martin Resch, 2025 archival study, doi 10.1007/s00191-025-00902-z (paywalled; not fetched)

stops.name: Wels, the electrical works
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The plant is named only in the Peneder and Resch study as relayed by the dossier; the underlying article could not be fetched, so the siting is carried as reported and not independently confirmed. Month and day set to order the segment.
stops.campa: In Upper Austria an electrical engineering plant is financed out of the bank's industrial book. It is the theory turned into machinery: purchasing power created against nothing but a banker's judgement, handed to men who intend to produce what is not being produced. The Austrian crown of 1922 is losing a third of its value in a season and is not a medium in which anybody can plan a production run. That the ventures fail is not in doubt, and the plant at Wels never reaches stable output. The one study that names it sits behind a paywall and was not read in this pass.
sources: Peneder and Resch, 2025, as relayed in the research dossier; article paywalled and not fetched

stops.name: Hainfeld, the porcelain insulators
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, on the same footing as Wels. The deceiving Czechoslovak investor is likewise carried from the unfetched Peneder and Resch study and is not confirmed. Month and day set to order the segment.
stops.campa: A second venture, porcelain insulators for the electrical trade, is sited in the Gölsen valley south of Vienna. Glass follows, and others after that. The Theorie has no equation for a Czechoslovak investor who lies about what he is putting in, or for a supervisory board that cannot read the accounts it is signing. The pattern is the same each time and it is the pattern of the book: the entrepreneur needs no capital of his own, he needs a banker willing to create purchasing power on his behalf.
sources: Peneder and Resch, 2025, as relayed in the research dossier; article paywalled and not fetched

stops.name: Vienna, the resignation
stops.date_confidence: attested to September 1924; day set to 01. The bank itself did not fail until 1926, per Deutsche Biographie's career table ('Biedermann-Bank, Wien, 1926 gescheitert'); sources that date the collapse to 1924 conflate the resignation with the failure.
stops.campa: The franc speculation of 1924 breaks on the Vienna bourse and takes the industrial book down with it. In September the board forces his resignation, and he walks out personally liable for debts that will take a decade of an American professor's salary to clear. He clears them, every schilling, when staying in Europe would have let him walk away. He is forty-one and has no post of any kind: no ministry, no bank, and no university, having given up the Graz chair for the bank. The bank goes on two more years without him and fails in 1926.
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net

stops.name: Vienna, questioned
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and the dossier tagged it wrongly as attested. No source consulted, and that includes Deutsche Biographie, en. and de.wikipedia, the HET profile and schumpeter.info, names Felix Braun-Stammfest, a negligent-insolvency proceeding, or Schumpeter's questioning as a suspect. The claim rests on the dossier alone. Month and day set to order the segment.
stops.campa: Investigators are said to have questioned him as a suspect in negligent-insolvency proceedings against a partner, Felix Braun-Stammfest, after the ventures went down. No indictment has been located and no conviction, and neither has the file that would show either. The absence of a record of charge is not a record of clearance and should not be read here as one. He is forty-two, and the debt he has undertaken to pay is the one thing about the year that nobody disputes.
sources: research dossier synthesis only; no independent corroboration in this pass

segments.name: Bonn: The Chair, the Marriage, the Two Graves

stops.name: Bonn, the chair of public finance
stops.date_confidence: attested to October 1925; day set to 01. German citizenship attested to 1925.
stops.campa: Arthur Spiethoff, who has been working for years to bring him to the Rhine, secures him the chair of public finance at Bonn, in the old electoral palace. Schumpeter takes German citizenship the same year. He arrives ruined, forty-two, and immediately builds the only school of students he will ever have: Wolfgang Stolper, August Lösch, Hans Wolfgang Singer, Kläre Tisch. He is a spectacular lecturer and an exhausting one, and he is at the same time revising the Theorie der wirtschaftlichen Entwicklung for the second edition of 1926.
suggested_refs: The Kurfürstliches Schloss, Bonn, seat of the university faculty
The Schumpeter School of Business and Economics at Bergische Universität Wuppertal, named for him in October 2008
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net

stops.name: Vienna, the concierge's daughter
stops.date_confidence: attested to 5 November 1925 and to Vienna; the specific church is not documented in any source consulted, so the coordinate is the city.
stops.campa: He converts to Lutheranism and marries Anna Josefina Reisinger, called Annie, the daughter of the concierge in his mother's Vienna apartment house. He is forty-two and has known her since she was a child on those stairs. The Theresianum-trained Herr Professor with a title, a wrecked bank and a ledger of debt marries down his own stairwell and is indifferent to who remarks on it. On when the first marriage legally ended, Deutsche Biographie says 1920, Wikipedia says 1925, and neither of them reproduces a document.

stops.name: Vienna, Johanna dies
stops.date_confidence: attested to 22 June 1926 by the dossier's chronology drawing on the standard biographies; the two fetched reference works agree on the year and on the closeness of the two deaths but not on the exact day-order.
stops.campa: His mother dies on the twenty-second of June. She had taken him out of Moravia to Graz, married a Feldmarschallleutnant to get him through the door of the Theresianum, and lived to see him a minister of state; every rung he climbed she had set under him first. He is forty-three. The reference works consulted agree on the year and not on the exact day-order of the deaths of that summer. The person around whom the whole ascent was organised is gone, and he is in Bonn among students who know him only as the man in the beautiful suits.
sources: research dossier chronology drawing on McCraw, Stolper and Swedberg

stops.name: Bonn, Annie and the child
stops.date_confidence: attested to 3 August 1926. The place is inferred from the couple's residence at Bonn in this period; the hospital or address is not documented in any source consulted.
stops.campa: Annie dies in childbirth on the third of August. The infant, a son named Joseph, dies with her. They have been married nine months; his mother has been dead six weeks. He is forty-three years old, and his private life ends here and is not resumed for eleven years. He keeps their room and their things exactly as they stood, and begins writing, in a diary he will keep for the rest of his life, to the two dead women, in a religiously charged language he uses nowhere else and in front of nobody.
sources: research dossier chronology drawing on McCraw, Stolper and Swedberg

stops.name: Harvard, the visiting years
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1927-1928 and 1930; month set to the start of the American term. Pin inherited byte-identical from david_rockefeller.journey.json.
stops.campa: Taussig brings him to Cambridge as a visitor for the academic year, and again in 1930. He teaches, he is liked, and the department begins to consider him as something to acquire permanently. He is forty-four, starting a second career on a continent he first saw as an exchange professor with a marriage collapsing behind him. He answers the wreckage of 1926 with work: the lecturing, the seminars, and the outside articles that go year after year against the Biedermann debt.
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net

stops.name: Tokyo University of Commerce, Kunitachi
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1931 by en.wikipedia, not by the HET profile the dossier cited, which contains no mention of Japan at all. No source fetched supports the dossier's January-February range, so month and day are set to 01. The institution was Tokyo University of Commerce (Tokyo Shoka Daigaku) from 1920 to 1944 and is now Hitotsubashi University; the campus moved to Kunitachi in 1927 after the Great Kanto earthquake, and the coordinate is within a few hundred metres of the present university.
stops.campa: He lectures in Japan on depression, on business cycles, on commercial policy, and on the state of economics as a science, to an audience that has been reading him in Japanese since the twenties and will go on reading him when Europe has stopped. The world is two years into the slump his Theorie says the system manufactures out of its own motion. He tells them what he tells everybody who asks: a depression is the mechanism working, not the mechanism broken, and the cure most governments reach for is an interference with the recovery.
stops.quote: In all cases, not only in the two which we have analyzed, recovery came of itself.
stops.quote_source: 'Depressions: Can We Learn from Past Experience?', in The Economics of the Recovery Program (1934)

stops.name: Harvard, the permanent chair
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1932; month set to the start of term. Pin inherited byte-identical from david_rockefeller.journey.json.
stops.campa: He takes the permanent Harvard professorship in 1932, before Hitler is in power and while the move is still a choice rather than a flight. He will hold the George F. Baker chair. A good part of the department finds him insufferable, and he is aware of it, and he does not modify anything. Leontief, Samuelson and Sweezy pass through his classroom; he lets students argue him down in public, promotes Keynesians whose conclusions he rejects, and refuses to build a faction out of the people who owe him.
suggested_refs: david_rockefeller.journey.json, stop 'Harvard College, economics in the pit of the Depression' (September 1932), which records Schumpeter's ideas as in the air at Cambridge during Rockefeller's undergraduate years and expressly flags no documented tutelage
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net

stops.name: New York, Elizabeth Boody Firuski
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1937 and to New York by Deutsche Biographie; the venue is not documented, the coordinate is a generic midtown point, and month and day are set to order the segment.
stops.campa: He marries Elizabeth Boody Firuski, an American economic historian of Japan, eleven years after Bonn. She takes over the running of his life: the house at Taconic in the Connecticut hills, the English prose he still writes as though translating himself out of German, the manuscripts, the correspondence, the appointments. Everything he publishes from here forward passes through her hands first, and the last book will not exist at all except through them. He makes his last visit to Europe the same year.

stops.name: Cambridge, citizenship and Business Cycles
stops.date_confidence: both attested to 1939; month and day set to 01. Pin inherited byte-identical from david_rockefeller.journey.json.
stops.campa: He becomes an American citizen and publishes Business Cycles in two volumes: theory, history and statistics together, three superimposed waves of different length tracked through a century and a half of capitalist production. It is the book he regards as his major work. He is fifty-six. Simon Kuznets takes it apart on the statistics; the profession, three years into the General Theory, has gone the other way and is not listening to a word of it. It sells badly.
stops.quote: As soon as we go into details and inquire into the individual items in which progress was most conspicuous, the trail leads not to the doors of those firms that work under conditions of comparatively free competition but precisely to the doors of the large concerns...
stops.quote_source: Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy (1942), ch. VII, p. 82; 'doors' plural in both the 1942 first edition and the Routledge text, against the singular that circulates
suggested_refs: Business Cycles: A Theoretical, Historical, and Statistical Analysis of the Capitalist Process, 2 vols. (1939)
sources: History of Economic Thought profile, hetwebsite.net

stops.name: Cambridge, the process of creative destruction
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1942; month and day set to 01. Pin inherited byte-identical from david_rockefeller.journey.json. The quotation was verified against the 1942 Harper first-edition text and the Routledge text-layer edition, ch. VII, p. 83.
stops.campa: In the seventh chapter of Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy he gives the mechanism its name and takes the word from biology to do it. The idea is thirty years old in his own work; it goes back to the circular flow he built at Czernowitz in order to break it. Competition that matters is not two firms undercutting each other on the price of the same article. It is the new commodity, the new technology, the new source of supply, the new form of organisation, striking not at the margins of existing firms but at their foundations and their lives.
stops.quote: This process of Creative Destruction is the essential fact about capitalism. It is what capitalism consists in and what every capitalist concern has got to live in...
stops.quote_source: Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy (Harper & Brothers, 1942), ch. VII, 'The Process of Creative Destruction'
suggested_refs: Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy, ch. VII, pp. 82-83, where the U.S. Steel sentence stands immediately before this one
The Economist's weekly 'Schumpeter' business column, begun 17 September 2009 and named for him

stops.name: Cambridge, can capitalism survive
stops.date_confidence: same volume, 1942, Part II prologue, p. 61; the date is set only to order the two stops within the one book. Wording verified in both the 1942 Harper first edition and the Routledge text: a period after 'No', not a comma, and the dossier's R tag on this quotation is upgraded to attested.
stops.campa: The prologue to the second part opens with the question and answers it in four words, then spends the rest of the paragraph telling the reader that the answer is of no interest whatever. His case is not that capitalism fails. It is that it succeeds: it delivers the goods, dissolves the aristocratic and family structures that had shielded it, produces an educated class with a professional interest in criticising it, and routinises innovation inside corporate research departments until the entrepreneur is a salaried employee and then no longer needed at all.
stops.quote: Can capitalism survive? No. I do not think it can. But this opinion of mine, like that of every other economist who has pronounced upon the subject, is in itself completely uninteresting. What counts in any attempt at social prognosis is not the Yes or No that sums up the facts and arguments which lead up to it but those facts and arguments themselves.
stops.quote_source: Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy (Harper & Brothers, 1942), Part II, Prologue, p. 61

stops.name: Cambridge, the federal file
stops.date_confidence: the investigation is placed in the war years by the dossier's synthesis of the FBI record, which was not independently re-checked in this pass; month and day set to order the segment. Pin inherited byte-identical from david_rockefeller.journey.json.
stops.campa: Federal agents open a file on the Schumpeters during the war. Elizabeth's scholarship on the Japanese economy is one prompt. His own view, stated freely at dinner tables and in seminars, that the Soviet Union is the greater long-term danger and that the war is being fought on the wrong side of the real question, is another. He goes on saying it in exactly the same rooms, to exactly the same people, for the rest of the war. They find no espionage and no Nazi affiliation, and they close the file.
sources: research dossier synthesis of the FBI-investigation record; not independently re-verified

stops.name: Cambridge, the two presidencies
stops.date_confidence: the AEA presidency is attested for 1948 by the association's own list of past officers; the International Economic Association designation is attested to 1949/1950 by the Crimson obituary. Month and day set to 01.
stops.campa: The American Economic Association elects him its president for 1948. He is sixty-five, honoured at last by the profession that had shelved Business Cycles, and he uses the platform to argue that the drift into socialism is not a policy anybody is choosing but a tendency inside the thing itself, and not one he expects to see reversed. The new International Economic Association makes him its first president the year after. He dies before presiding over a single meeting of it.
stops.quote: This civilization is rapidly passing away, however.
stops.quote_source: 'The March into Socialism', American Economic Review, 1949/1950
suggested_refs: American Economic Association, list of past presidents: 'JOSEPH A. SCHUMPETER, Harvard, 1948'

stops.name: Taconic, Salisbury, the country house
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Crimson obituary, which gives 'early Sunday morning'; 8 January 1950 was a Sunday. The coordinate is Salisbury's own, the hamlet of Taconic having no separately published coordinate; the dossier's geography lens carried a longitude some 7.5 km east of this and contradicted its own afterlife lens, whose value is the correct one and is used here.
stops.campa: He works through the autumn of 1949, then goes out to the house in the Connecticut hills to rest and to prepare the Walgreen Lectures he is to give at Chicago. In the early hours of Sunday the eighth of January he dies in his sleep of a cerebral hemorrhage. He is sixty-six. On the desk is the manuscript of the History of Economic Analysis, nine years' work and unfinished: the whole of the subject told not as a body of results but as the record of how it came to be thought. The Walgreen Lectures are not given.
stops.quote: The first thing a man will do for his ideals is lie.
stops.quote_source: History of Economic Analysis (Oxford University Press, 1954), p. 43
suggested_refs: The unfinished manuscript of History of Economic Analysis, completed and published by Elizabeth Boody Schumpeter in 1954

stops.name: St. John's, Salisbury, the funeral
stops.date_confidence: attested. The obituary of 9 January announced services 'tomorrow at 2 p.m.', that is, two days after the death and not the next day as the dossier's afterlife entry stated.
stops.campa: The funeral is held at two in the afternoon on the tenth of January at the Episcopal church in Salisbury, two days after the death, with a separate memorial service set for Cambridge. Where he was afterwards buried the obituary does not say, and none of the reference works consulted names a cemetery or a grave. The Moravian manufacturer's son, Austrian finance minister, German professor and American citizen has a documented funeral and no documented interment. That is a hole in the accessible record, not a fact about him.
suggested_refs: St. John's Episcopal Church, Salisbury, Connecticut
sources: en.wikipedia.org and de.wikipedia.org, 'Joseph Schumpeter', both silent on burial

stops.name: Memorial Church, Harvard Yard, the sentence everybody had heard
stops.date_confidence: the memorial service at Harvard is attested to January 1950 by the obituary, which gives no day; the date is set to order the segment. The quotation is printed by the Crimson on 10 January 1950 as a direct first-person quotation, in this wording and this order, lover then horseman then economist; the underlying oral tradition, and which of the three he meant, remain tradition.
stops.campa: The university holds its service for him in the Yard. Two days after the death the student paper had already printed the sentence that everybody who knew him had heard him produce, in one wording or another, for forty years. Wieser's and Böhm-Bawerk's student had ridden in Hyde Park and had been challenged over library books in Bukovina, and the whole architecture of the joke is that he never would say. Which of the three did he fail at? The sentence does not tell. Neither did he.
stops.quote: In my youth, my ambition was to be the greatest lover in Vienna, the greatest horseman in Austria, and the greatest economist in the world. In one of those goals I have failed.
